extracted.intended_audience: Worldcon members, Hugo nominators/voters, and potential nominees (authors, editors, artists, publishers)
extracted.subtask_description: Plain-English interpretation of the WSFS Constitution rules defining Hugo Award categories and eligibility (who/what is eligible, timing, length thresholds, professional vs fan distinctions, and special-case rules). Intended to guide nominators, voters, and potential nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Award Category
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three main types of Hugo Award category: Individual works (e.g., a single book or film), People (the Award is given for the work that person has done in the year of eligibility), and Serial publications (the Award is given for the entire run of that publication in the year of eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For people categories note the 'year of eligibility' qualification — a famous person who produced no work in the eligibility year should not be nominated. For serial publications the Award is for the run in the year, not a single issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year of Eligibility — basic rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All Awards are given for work in a given year. Individual works are eligible only in their first year of publication. For people and serial publications the Award is given for all achievements in the year in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The year is from the printed publication date if there is one, or else from the copyright date. Note the Awards are labeled for the year they are presented (e.g., 2019 Hugos generally for works first published in 2018). The WSFS Business Meeting can extend eligibility of particular works (such extensions will be printed with nominating ballot information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Country & Language of Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are eligible when they are first published. They can be published anywhere in the world and in any language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works first published in a language other than English are eligible in their first year of publication in English translation. Works published in prior years outside the USA are eligible if they were published for the first time in the USA in the current year (to account for US-based nominator visibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serialized Works eligibility and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual elements of a multi-part story arc are always eligible for their year of publication; voters may nominate a complete story arc, in which case the publication date of the final installment of the series counts for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual installment of a story arc achieves a nomination on its own then the complete story arc will probably be ruled ineligible if nominated, because voters have indicated the installment stands on its own. The same applies if book 1 of a trilogy is nominated on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web Sites, E-books, and Medium of Distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that a work be published on paper — publishing and distributing your work on a web site is exactly the same as having copies of your book in a bookstore or your movie shown in a theatre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medium of distribution has nothing to do with a work’s eligibility. If a work is first published electronically and then printed without substantial revisions in a later year, the later paper publication is not a new work — the original electronic publication is what’s eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Published Works
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no restriction on who publishes a work; self-published novels available on a web site or printed at the author's expense are eligible just the same as traditionally published novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-publication does not disadvantage eligibility for written/graphic fiction and non-fiction Hugo categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of Work — guidance for nominators
rubrics_metrics.description: Several of the category definitions are based on the length of a work. If you haven't counted the number of words, check recommendation lists or guess; administrators will generally move nominations into the correct category if you have them wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt consult recommendation lists linked on the site, or contact the administrators who can help or reassign nominations to the correct category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Novel (length threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for a science fiction or fantasy story of forty thousand (40,000) words or more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Novella (length threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for a science fiction or fantasy story of between seventeen thousand five hundred (17,500) and forty thousand (40,000) words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Novelette (length threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for a science fiction or fantasy story of between seven thousand five hundred (7,500) and seventeen thousand five hundred (17,500) words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Short Story (length threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for a science fiction or fantasy story of less than seven thousand five hundred (7,500) words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for multi-installment works appearing in at least three installments with a total of at least 240,000 words. A qualifying installment must be published in the qualifying year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installments of a series can be of any length (do not have to be novel-length). Once a Series wins the Award, it is no longer eligible even if further installments appear. If a Series is a finalist and does not win, it is no longer eligible until at least two more installments totalling at least 240,000 words appear in subsequent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Graphic Story or Comic
rubrics_metrics.description: A science fiction or fantasy story told in graphic form, such as a comic book, graphic novel, or webcomic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Related Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to a work related to the field of science fiction, fantasy, or fandom, appearing for the first time during the previous calendar year or which has been substantially modified during the previous calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible works include collections of art, works of literary criticism, books about the making of a film or TV series, biographies, etc., provided they do not qualify for another category. Specifically, the Constitution says any work in this category must be 'either non-fiction or, if fictional, is noteworthy primarily for aspects other than the fictional text, and which is not eligible in any other category.' Fiction anthologies generally are not eligible here because the individual works are eligible in the story categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dramatic Presentation (Long Form)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Award can be given to a dramatized production in any medium. The work must last 90 minutes or longer (excluding commercials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediums include film, television, radio, live theater, computer games, or music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dramatic Presentation (Short Form)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Award can be given to a dramatized production in any medium. The work must be less than 90 minutes long (excluding commercials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Editor (Long Form) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible the person must have edited at least 4 novel-length (i.e. 40,000 words or more) books devoted to science fiction and/or fantasy in the year of eligibility that are not anthologies or collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a person category; the Award is given for the work that person has done in the year of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Editor (Short Form) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible the person must have edited at least four anthologies, collections or magazine issues devoted to science fiction and/or fantasy, at least one of which must have been published in the year of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional publication definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A professional publication either (1) provided at least a quarter the income of any one person or, (2) was owned or published by any entity which provided at least a quarter the income of any of its staff and/or owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used only to distinguish Best Professional Artist vs Best Fan Artist and to define Semiprozine vs Fanzine. It does not affect written-fiction categories like Best Novel or Best Short Story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Professional Artist
rubrics_metrics.description: Person category for artists and illustrators; the work on which the nominees are judged must class as 'professional' (see professional publication definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Semiprozine
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify, the publication must have produced at least 4 issues, at least one of which must have appeared in the year of eligibility, and must not be professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A semiprozine must meet at least one of the following criteria: the publication pays its contributors and/or staff in other than copies of the publication; or the publication was generally available only for paid purchase. Semiprozine is intended to separate small semi-professional magazines from fanzines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Fanzine
rubrics_metrics.description: This Award is for anything that is neither professional nor semi-professional and that does not qualify as a Fancast. The publication must also have produced at least 4 issues, at least one of which must have appeared in the year of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Fancast
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for any non-professional audio- or video-casting with at least four (4) episodes that had at least one (1) episode released in the previous calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Fan Writer — scope of considered work
rubrics_metrics.description: Person category for fan writers. Work published in fanzines, semiprozines, and even on mailing lists, blogs, BBSs, and similar electronic fora can be included when judging this Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only work in professional publications should not be considered for Best Fan Writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Fan Artist — scope of considered work
rubrics_metrics.description: Person category for fan artists. Eligible work is not limited to material published in fanzines; material for semiprozines or public displays (such as convention art shows) is also eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fan artists can have work published in professional publications as well, but you should not consider professionally-published works when judging this award.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Lodestar Award — status and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lodestar Award for Best Young Adult Book is not a Hugo Award. It is voted for and presented by WSFS alongside the Hugo Awards, and its rules are set in the WSFS Constitution. It is for a book published for young adult readers in the field of science fiction and fantasy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it is not a Hugo Award, a work can be eligible for the Lodestar Award and for the corresponding Hugo Award (based on length) in the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Astounding Award — status and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Astounding Award for Best New Writer is not a Hugo Award; it is voted for and presented alongside the Hugo Awards, but its eligibility rules are not governed by the WSFS Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dell Magazines specifies eligibility: limited to authors whose first SFWA-eligible publication occurred within the two years prior to the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Hugo Award categories (Worldcon discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Worldcon Committees have the right to add one extra Hugo Award category each year; these extra categories are not permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is intended for special circumstances rather than regular use; generally no additional awards are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Awards (committee discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Worldcons give out special awards during the Hugo Awards ceremony. These awards are at the committee’s discretion, rather than by general vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such special awards may not use the Hugo Award rocket and are not considered Hugo Awards, though they may be listed alongside Hugos because presented at the same ceremony.
